'''''Galega orientalis''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[Fabaceae]], the [[legume]] family.<ref name=":0" /> It is known commonly as '''fodder galega''' and '''eastern galega'''. It is cultivated as a [[fodder]] and [[forage]] for [[livestock]].

This species is native to the [[Caucasus]].<ref name=fao>Frame, J. [http://www.fao.org/ag/agp/AGPC/doc/Gbase/data/pf000480.htm ''Galega orientalis'' Lam.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407101727/http://www.fao.org/ag/AGP/AGPC/doc/Gbase/DATA/Pf000480.HTM |date=2014-04-07 }} Grassland Species Profiles. FAO.</ref> Its native range includes parts of [[Russia]], [[Armenia]], and [[Azerbaijan]]. It has been [[introduced species|introduced]] to many other regions for use in agriculture.<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate = 21 January 2018}}</ref>

== Taxonomy ==
It was first described in 1788 by [[Jean-Baptiste Lamarck]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=''Galega orientalis'' Lam. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:495682-1 |access-date=2025-08-19 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref><ref name=Lamarck>{{cite Q|Q5832503|volume=2|issue=2|date=1788|pages=596| url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/721250}} </ref>

==Description==
This species is a perennial herb with a [[taproot]] and [[rhizome]] system. It produces stems up to {{convert|2|m|ftin}} tall which branch near the middle. The leaves are [[pinnate]]. The [[inflorescence]] bears up to 70 [[lilac (color)|lilac-colored]] flowers,<ref name=fao/> and some [[cultivar]]s can produce more.<ref name=bale2>Baležentienė, L. (2008). [http://llufb.llu.lv/conference/agrvestis/content/n10/AgrVestis-Nr10-82-87.pdf Bio-morphological peculiarities of new cultivars of fodder galega (''Galega orientalis'' Lam.)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303233544/http://llufb.llu.lv/conference/agrvestis/content/n10/AgrVestis-Nr10-82-87.pdf |date=2016-03-03 }} ''Agronomijas Vēstis'' 10 82-7.</ref> The fruit pod is up to {{convert|4|cm|in}} long and contains up to 8 seeds each a few millimeters in length.<ref name=fao/>

==Biology==
The plant can grow on a variety of soil types, performing best on deep, light, [[friability|friable]], well-drained, higher-[[pH]] soils. It is quite tolerant of winter cold, but late-season frosts can damage fresh growth. It is somewhat tolerant of [[drought]] and flooding. It does not do as well on acidic, [[peat]]y, or water-logged soils. It responds well to supplemental phosphorus and potassium.<ref name=agro>[http://www.agroatlas.ru/en/content/cultural/Galega_orientalis_K/ ''Galega orientalis'' Lam.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150506000730/http://www.agroatlas.ru/en/content/cultural/Galega_orientalis_K/ |date=2015-05-06 }} AgroAtlas: Interactive Agricultural Ecological Atlas of Russia and Neighboring Countries.</ref>

Like many other legumes, it [[nitrogen-fixation|fixes nitrogen]].<ref name=agro/> Its root nodule bacterium is  ''[[Rhizobium galegae]]''. Growers must ensure that their seed has been inoculated with it to produce adequate plant growth.<ref name=fao/> Some strains of ''R. galegae'' are more effective [[symbiosis|symbionts]] than others, and different strains compete on one plant. When a less effective strain outcompetes effective strains, the plant does not grow as well.<ref name=tas>Tas, E., et al. (1996). [http://aem.asm.org/content/62/2/529.full.pdf Assessment of competitiveness of rhizobia infecting ''Galega orientalis'' on the basis of plant yield, nodulation, and strain identification by antibiotic resistance and PCR.] ''Applied and Environmental Microbiology'' 62(2) 529-35.</ref>

The rhizome of the plant makes it persistent in the field; the rhizome spreads, sending up new stems, and the plant can live well over ten years,<ref name=agro/> even exceeding 30 years in some areas.<ref name=adam>Adamovics, A., et al. (2011). [http://www.egf2011.at/files/pubs/416_adamovics.pdf Biogas production from ''Galega orientalis'' Lam. and galega-grass biomass.]{{Dead link|date=December 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} ''Grassland Science in Europe'' 16 416-18.</ref>

==Ecology==
The flowers are [[pollination|pollinated]] by [[bee]]s.<ref name=fao/> It produces good quantities of [[nectar]] and [[pollen]].<ref name=agro/> It makes a good [[honey|honey plant]].<ref name=raig>Raig, H., et al. [http://www.eria.ee/public/files/Fodder_Galega_lk_5_53.pdf ''Fodder Galega''.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070705230910/http://www.eria.ee/public/files/Fodder_Galega_lk_5_53.pdf |date=2007-07-05 }} Eesti Maaviljeluse Instituut, Estonia. 2001.</ref>

The plant is host to several [[fungus|fungal]] species, some pathogenic, such as ''[[Ascochyta]]'' sp., which causes [[blight]], ''[[Fusarium oxysporum]]'', which causes [[Fusarium wilt]], and the gray mould ''[[Botrytis cinerea]]''. Other species include ''[[Humicola brevis]]'', ''[[Acremonium strictum]]'', and ''[[Cladosporium cladosporioides]]''.<ref name=cwal>Cwalina-Ambroziak, B. and J. Koc. (2005). [https://pbsociety.org.pl/journals/index.php/aa/article/view/1894 Fungi colonising the above-ground parts of fodder galega (''Galega orientalis'' Lam.) cultivated in pure sowing and mixed with smooth brome-grass (''Bromus inermis'' Leyss.)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171202232902/https://pbsociety.org.pl/journals/index.php/aa/article/view/1894 |date=2017-12-02 }} ''Acta Agrobotanica'' 58(1).</ref>

==Uses==
This plant is grown to feed livestock. Its potential value as a fodder was first suggested in 1908, and trials began near [[Moscow]] in the 1920s.<ref name=raig/> It is productive, persistent, and nutritious, with high protein.<ref name=agro/> It contains high levels of [[carotene]], [[dietary mineral|minerals]], and [[vitamin]]s, especially [[vitamin C]].<ref name=bale>Baležentienė, L. and V. Spruogis. (2011). [http://vetzoo.lva.lt/data/vols/2011/56/pdf/balezentiene.pdf Experience of fodder galega (''Galega orientalis'' Lam.) and traditional fodder grasses use for forage production in organic farm.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140606213901/http://vetzoo.lva.lt/data/vols/2011/56/pdf/balezentiene.pdf |date=2014-06-06 }} ''Veterinarija ir Zootechnika'' 56 78.</ref> It produces many crops of vegetation, its rhizome continuing to produce stems as it grows. It can be cut down repeatedly and taken for [[hay]] and [[silage]], and the stubble can be [[grazing|grazed]]. The whole plant is not generally suitable for grazing, though. It works well as a [[companion planting|companion]] to a non-competitive [[grass]] such as [[Timothy-grass|timothy]] or [[festuca|fescue]].<ref name=agro/> In cold northern regions it is valuable because it produces vegetation earlier in the spring and continues later in the fall than some other forages.<ref name=bale/> It is low in [[toxin|toxic]] [[alkaloid]] concentration, making it useful as feed when its alkaloid-rich close relative ''[[Galega officinalis]]'' is not.<ref name=raig/>

The cultivar 'Gale', developed jointly by [[Estonia]]n and Russian breeders, was released in 1987.<ref name=fao/> The cultivars 'Vidmantai', 'Laukiai', and 'Melsviai' have been bred in [[Lithuania]].<ref name=bale2/>

The plant has been investigated as a source of [[biogas]], and it has produced a good amount in trials when mixed with grasses and [[manure]].<ref name=adam/>

It has been tested as an agent of [[bioremediation]] of oil-polluted soils. Some of the bacteria it hosts can degrade soil pollutants such as [[toluene]]s.<ref name=kak>Kaksonen, A. H., et al. (2006). [http://www.dzumenvis.nic.in/General%20Ecology/pdf/Rhizosphere%20effect%20of%20Galega.pdf Rhizosphere effect of ''Galega orientalis'' in oil-contaminated soil.]{{Dead link|date=December 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} ''Soil Biology and Biochemistry'' 38(4) 817-27.</ref>

It is also grown as an [[ornamental plant]] in [[garden]]s.<ref name=bourne>Bourne, V. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/gardening/5602944/How-to-grow-Galega-orientalis.html How to grow: ''Galega orientalis''.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121011025803/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/gardening/5602944/How-to-grow-Galega-orientalis.html |date=2012-10-11 }} ''[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]''. June 22, 2009.</ref>

The plant has also been considered a prospective [[energy crop]].
